context:
POST /api/v2/team/{team_id}/group
This endpoint creates a [User Group](https://docs.clickup.com/en/articles/4010016-teams-how-to-create-user-groups) within a Workspace.\ \ User Groups are used to organize and manage users within a Workspace.\ \ In the API documentation, `team_id` refers to the Workspace ID, and `group_id` refers to the User Group ID.\ \ **Note:** Adding a guest with view-only permissions to a Team automatically converts them to a paid guest.\ \ If no paid guest seats are available, an additional member seat will be added, increasing the number of paid guest seats.\ \ This change incurs a prorated charge based on the billing cycle.
Required: team_id (path) — Workspace ID; body (body)

name: Get Filtered Team Tasks
description: Get Filtered Team Tasks View the tasks that meet specific criteria from a Workspace. GET /api/v2/team/{team_Id}/task
context:
GET /api/v2/team/{team_Id}/task
View the tasks that meet specific criteria from a Workspace. Responses are limited to 100 tasks per page. \ \ You can only view task information of tasks you can access. \ \ Each task's `custom_fields` array only includes Custom Fields applicable to that task's `custom_item_id`.\ \ Our Try It modal currently supports filtering by two or more Lists, Folders, or Spaces. To filter by a single List, Folder, or Space, we recommend using a free app like [Postman](https://www.postman.com/) to test our public API.
Required: team_Id (path) — Workspace ID
Optional: page (query) — Page to fetch (starts at 0).; order_by (query) — Order by a particular field. By default, tasks are ordered by `created`.\ \ Options include: `id`, `created`, `updated`, and `due_date`.; reverse (query) — Tasks are displayed in reverse order.; subtasks (query) — Include or exclude subtasks. By default, subtasks are excluded.; space_ids[] (query) — Filter by Spaces. For example: \ \ `?space_ids[]=1234&space_ids[]=6789`; project_ids[] (query) — Filter by Folders. For example: \ \ `?project_ids[]=1234&project_ids[]=6789`; list_ids[] (query) — Filter by Lists. For example: \ \ `?list_ids[]=1234&list_ids[]=6789`; statuses[] (query) — Filter by statuses. Use `%20` to represent a space character. To include closed tasks, use the `include_closed` parameter. \ \ For example: \ \ `?statuses[]=to%20do&statuses[]=in%20progress`; include_closed (query) — Include or excluse closed tasks. By default, they are excluded.\ \ To include closed tasks, use `include_closed: true`.; assignees[] (query) — Filter by Assignees using people's ClickUp user id. For example: \ \ `?assignees[]=1234&assignees[]=5678`; tags[] (query) — Filter by tags. User `%20` to represent a space character. For example: \ \ `?tags[]=tag1&tags[]=this%20tag`; due_date_gt (query) — Filter by due date greater than Unix time in milliseconds.; due_date_lt (query) — Filter by due date less than Unix time in milliseconds.; date_created_gt (query) — Filter by date created greater than Unix time in milliseconds.; date_created_lt (query) — Filter by date created less than Unix time in milliseconds.; date_updated_gt (query) — Filter by date updated greater than Unix time in milliseconds.; date_updated_lt (query) — Filter by date updated less than Unix time in milliseconds.; date_done_gt (query) — Filter by date done greater than Unix time in milliseconds.; date_done_lt (query) — Filter by date done less than Unix time in milliseconds.; custom_fields (query) — Include tasks with specific values in one or more Custom Fields. Custom Relationships are included.\ \ For example: `?custom_fields=[{"field_id":"abcdefghi12345678","operator":"=","value":"1234"}{"field_id":"jklmnop123456","operator":"<","value":"5"}]`\ \ Only set Custom Field values display in the `value` property of the `custom_fields` parameter. The `=` operator isn't supported with Label Custom Fields.\ \ Learn more about [filtering using Custom Fields.](doc:taskfilters); parent (query) — Include the parent task ID to return subtasks.; include_markdown_description (query) — To return task descriptions in Markdown format, use `?include_markdown_description=true`.; custom_items[] (query) — Filter by custom task types. For example: \ \ `?custom_items[]=0&custom_items[]=1300` \ \ Including `0` returns tasks. Including `1` returns Milestones. Including any other number returns the custom task type as defined in your Workspace.

name: Get Workspace Custom Fields
description: Get Workspace Custom Fields View the Custom Fields you have access to in a specific Workspace. GET /api/v2/team/{team_id}/field
context:
GET /api/v2/team/{team_id}/field
View the Custom Fields you have access to in a specific Workspace. Get Workspace Custom Fields only returns Custom Fields created at the Workspace level. Custom Fields created at the Space, Folder, and List level are not included.\ \ Custom Fields scoped to specific custom task types include an `applied_objects` array on each field object. Each entry has `object_type` (`19` for custom task type) and `object_id` (the custom task type ID, matching `custom_item_id` on tasks). Use [Get Custom Task Types](ref:getcustomitems) to resolve IDs to names. Fields without task-type scoping omit `applied_objects`.
Required: team_id (path) — Workspace ID; Content-Type (header)
Optional: include_applied_objects (query) — When `true`, includes `applied_objects` on task-type-scoped Custom Fields in the response.

name: Get time entries within a date range
description: Get time entries within a date range View time entries filtered by start and end date. GET /api/v2/team/{team_Id}/time_entries
context:
GET /api/v2/team/{team_Id}/time_entries
View time entries filtered by start and end date. \ \ By default, this endpoint returns time entries from the last 30 days created by the authenticated user. \ \ To retrieve time entries for other users, you must include the `assignee` query parameter. \ \ Only one of the following location filters can be included at a time: `space_id`, `folder_id`, `list_id`, or `task_id`. \ \ ***Note:** A time entry that has a negative duration means that timer is currently running for that user.*
Required: team_Id (path) — Workspace ID; Content-Type (header)
Optional: start_date (query) — Unix time in milliseconds; end_date (query) — Unix time in milliseconds; assignee (query) — Filter by `user_id`. For multiple assignees, separate `user_id` using commas.\ \ **Example:** `assignee=1234,9876`\ \ ***Note:** Only Workspace Owners/Admins have access to do this.*; include_task_tags (query) — Include task tags in the response for time entries associated with tasks.; include_location_names (query) — Include the names of the List, Folder, and Space along with the `list_id`,`folder_id`, and `space_id`.; include_approval_history (query) — Include the history of the approval for each time entry. Adds status changes, notes, and approvers.; include_approval_details (query) — Include the details of the approval for each time entry. Adds Approver ID, Approved Time, List of Approvers, and Approval Status.; space_id (query) — Only include time entries associated with tasks in a specific Space.; folder_id (query) — Only include time entries associated with tasks in a specific Folder.; list_id (query) — Only include time entries associated with tasks in a specific List.; task_id (query) — Only include time entries associated with a specific task.; custom_task_ids (query) — If you want to reference a task by it's custom task id, this value must be `true`.; team_id (query) — When the `custom_task_ids` parameter is set to `true`, the Workspace ID must be provided using the `team_id` parameter. \ For example: `custom_task_ids=true&team_id=123`.; is_billable (query) — Include only billable time entries by using a value of `true` or only non-billable time entries by using a value of `false`.\ \ For example: `?is_billable=true`.
